mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a supply-side expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo MA and HOUST > 12-mo MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly positive at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months, combined with a federal funds rate above 4%, signals disinflation under restrictive policy, which historically precedes equity market corrections and negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months AND FEDFUNDS > 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months, in conjunction with an unemployment rate below 4%, signals a tight labor market that boosts wage growth and inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo MA for two months AND UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly positive at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a broad-based supply contraction, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-mo MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 90% confidence.
